correctness.rationale: In the x=1 chart the gradient at P is (e,0,0). On e=0 the Hessian determinant is exactly 2c(ab-cf). On D=0 its kernel is generated by (-c,b,a), and the cubic restriction is ab(ah+bg-cd)t^3. The adapted coordinates have nondegenerate transverse Hessian determinant -a^2. When T=0, solving the transverse critical equations to the required order gives reduced quartic coefficient -b^2gh/(a^2c), nonzero under abcgh != 0. The analytic splitting lemma therefore yields A1, A2, A3 in the three stated cases. The bundled exact verifier reconstructs every algebraic identity.

The exact A1/A2/A3 refinement identifies the first two intrinsic degeneration equations inside that natural boundary and proves the terminal A3 order under a transparent nonvanishing condition. This is a structural local description of a standard explicit cubic-surface normal form, not an arbitrary parameter slice or a recomputation of a listed table.
